(1) critical food literacy is a necessary skill for engaging in public, democratic food systems discourse and for creating just, sustainable, food systems; (2) multicultural texts are one way of making visible the people who feed us, especially the workers who are less visible in food systems discourse; and (3) pedagogical strategies that engage multicultural texts can cultivate critical food literacy in learners.
